answer: A marble registry ties each identity to a salted hash of its funding source, and the bond grows quadratically: the first identity costs 10 POA, the tenth 1,000, the hundredth 100,000. An attacker building a thousand fakes faces a bond bill dwarfing any reward, while an honest user pays only the base bond once. A plume of random audits re-checks clusters each epoch; a cluster caught farming loses its bond and its bridge of referrals collapses. Limits: a wealthy attacker can still afford a small farm, and clustering can misfire on shared exchange wallets, so appeals and allowlisting are needed.
